verdict: NOT VERIFIABLE — the reference design holds in the lab (16/16 drill cases, 13/13 attacks rejected), but the live platform's agent-authentication controls cannot be confirmed from any public source.

findings.title: No published agent-authentication specification for the live platform
findings.evidence: The public Task Node page describes the lifecycle (request, work, evidence, reward) and the agent connect flow (link + short code approval), but publishes no token format, signing scheme, credential scope, or verification rule. docs.postfiat.org is a Notion page that returns no readable content to a plain fetch. Whether agent actions are signed at all is UNVERIFIED (C-31).
findings.remediation: Publish the agent credential format, the signing scheme, token lifetimes, and the revocation procedure; adopt the reference design in docs/auth-design.md.

findings.title: Reference design rejects 13/13 attack cases in the lab drill
findings.evidence: Drill D-01..D-16: 3 valid actions accepted, 13 attacks rejected with the expected reason (replay, forgery, tampering, escalation, cross-task reuse, expiry, revocation, stale/future timestamps, malformed action, untrusted issuer, nonce reuse, oversized payload). outputs/derived/drill-results.json, outputs/drill-run.log.
findings.remediation: None for the design. The gap is adoption: the design must be implemented and published by the platform, and its live behaviour independently verified.

findings.title: A single long-lived agent credential is a single point of compromise
findings.evidence: OWASP ASI03 (Identity and Privilege Abuse): agents inherit or escalate high-privilege credentials; the 2025 Agentic Top 10 lists credential leakage letting agents operate far beyond intended scope. The design counters it with per-task scoped, 1-hour tokens (docs/auth-design.md §3).
findings.remediation: Issue per-task, short-lived capability tokens only; never hand an agent a standing credential that authorizes more than one task.

findings.title: Forged evidence is rejected by signature verification
findings.evidence: D-05: an action claiming the victim's identity but signed with the attacker's key is rejected (bad-agent-signature). D-06: a valid signature over a different payload is rejected (payload-mismatch). Ed25519 verification is the binding mechanism; the implementation passes RFC 8032 TEST 1–3.
findings.remediation: Keep evidence signatures mandatory; never accept evidence whose payload hash was not signed by the task owner.

findings.title: Cross-task capability reuse is rejected
findings.evidence: D-08: a token issued for task-lab-001 presented on task-lab-002 is rejected (task-mismatch). The token binds task_id and the verifier compares it with the action's task_id.
findings.remediation: Bind every credential to exactly one task id at issuance; reject mismatches at verification.

findings.title: Goal hijack via poisoned task text is not stopped by cryptography
findings.evidence: OWASP ASI01 (Agent Goal Hijack) / LLM01 (Prompt Injection): malicious content alters the agent's objectives through its planning and reasoning. Signatures authenticate WHO acted, not WHETHER the objective was the requester's. No drill case covers it: it is a content attack, not a protocol attack.
findings.remediation: Content provenance for task text; treat linked documents as data, not instructions; require human approval for consequential actions.

findings.title: Revocation list blocks stolen-credential reuse
findings.evidence: D-10: after the agent is added to the revocation list, its previously valid token is rejected (agent-revoked). The check runs on every verification, before the capability check.
findings.remediation: Operate the revocation list as a live service with a stated maximum propagation delay; audit every revocation (docs/incident-response.md).

findings.title: No published credential revocation/rotation procedure for agents
findings.evidence: The public Task Node page documents device revocation ('Every connected device is listed, and can be revoked') but publishes no agent-credential revocation, rotation, or expiry procedure. Whether one exists is UNVERIFIED (C-33).
findings.remediation: Publish the rotation schedule, the revocation endpoint, and the maximum propagation delay; adopt docs/credential-lifecycle.md.

findings.title: Replay window is bounded by nonce cache plus a 300 s clock-skew window
findings.evidence: D-11 (stale timestamp) and D-12 (future timestamp) are rejected; D-04/D-15 (nonce reuse) are rejected. Design parameters: action TTL 900 s, clock skew 300 s, nonce cache retention 900 s; worst-case acceptance age 1,200 s. Nonce collision probability at 1e6 actions/day is 1.469e-27 (auth-model.json).
findings.remediation: Keep the windows as specified; alert on nonce cache saturation (a sign of replay flooding).

findings.title: Ed25519 fits the platform's existing key types
findings.evidence: postfiatd KeyType has exactly two values, secp256k1 and ed25519 (include/xrpl/protocol/KeyType.h:28–31, pinned 0085a1ff). Signing and verification dispatch by KeyType (SecretKey.h:175–180, PublicKey.h:241–252). A 64-byte Ed25519 signature is 12.5% of the 512-byte manifest cap (ManifestMessages.h:24).
findings.remediation: Use Ed25519 agent keys: they reuse the platform's existing key handling and fit every size budget.

findings.title: Per-task audit record must be append-only; its tamper-evidence is unverified
findings.evidence: The public Task Node page states each task has a requester, an owner, evidence and a verifier, and the record is public. Whether that record is tamper-evident (hash-chained or signed) is not published and is UNTESTABLE from outside (C-35).
findings.remediation: Hash-chain the per-task record and sign each entry with the platform key so any later edit is detectable.

findings.title: Reference implementation passes RFC 8032 test vectors 1–3
findings.evidence: Pure-Python Ed25519 (stdlib only) passes public-key derivation, signature production, verification, and tamper rejection for TEST 1 (empty message), TEST 2 (1 byte), TEST 3 (2 bytes). outputs/ed25519-test-vectors.log, 3/3 PASS in 3.76 s.
findings.remediation: None. The implementation is a reference, not a production library: it is slow (~0.85 s per sign) and makes no side-channel guarantees.
